exact.В семидесятом впервые разрешили развод,: In '70 divorce was allowed for the first time, and in '74 there was a referendum on whether to abolish it. Almost sixty per cent said keep it, and in some families people at the same table voted differently.
exact.Развод стал возможен, и даже тем, кто о: Divorce became possible, and even people who never thought about it felt somehow they had more room.
exact.Знакомые пары ругались как раньше, тольк: Couples we knew rowed just as before, only now someone would sometimes add, "Careful, it's allowed now." Most of them stayed together all the same, but the phrase stuck.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, поменяли семейно: When I was little, family law was changed and husband and wife became equal before the law. I only found out later.
exact.Поменяли семейное право, и муж с женой с: Family law was changed, and husband and wife became equal before the law. We girls joked that now they'd take turns doing the washing-up.
exact.В семьдесят пятом поменяли семейное прав: In '75 family law was changed: the husband was no longer the head over his wife, and both parents decided about the children. On paper everyone was equal, but at home each got used to it in their own way, some quickly, some never.
exact.Общее имущество супругов стало правилом,: Joint property for married couples became the rule, and "ours" came up more often when people talked about money.
exact.Многое из этого в хороших семьях было и: In good families a lot of that was already there, just not on paper. Where it wasn't, the paper didn't help straight away, but it helped.
exact.Потом лиры заменили на евро. Мне это объ: Later the lira was replaced by the euro. They explained it to me at length, and I still counted in lire.
exact.Лиры заменили на евро, и все долго перес: The lira was replaced by the euro, and for a long time everyone converted prices back into lire.
exact.Первого января в кошельках появились евр: On the first of January there were euros in our purses instead of lire. For a long time I converted everything back into lire, and that made prices seem either laughable or outrageous.
exact.К весне лиры перестали принимать, а в го: By spring the shops stopped taking lire, but in my head I counted in them for years.
exact.За один евро давали почти две тысячи лир: One euro was worth nearly two thousand lire, so at first everything seemed to cost next to nothing. Then I began to suspect the market stalls had worked that out too.
exact.Тогда пришла новая болезнь, и во всей ст: Then a new illness came, and the whole country went into lockdown.
exact.Весной по всей стране объявили карантин,: In the spring the whole country went into lockdown, and everyone stayed at home.
exact.В марте во всей стране объявили карантин: In March the whole country went into lockdown. The streets emptied, and I talked to my neighbour across the balcony more than in all the years before.

exact.Первым очагом тогда стал Кодоньо, в Ломб: The first outbreak was in Codogno, in Lombardy, and then the lockdown shut the whole country. What frightened me wasn't so much for myself as not being able to visit anyone.
exact.Когда Арно вышла из берегов, вода пришла: When the Arno burst its banks, the water came into the city where nobody expected it. For a long time afterwards, walking down a street, people would show each other how high it had come.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в ноябре шес: Later I was told how the Arno flooded Florence in November '66.

exact.Мне потом рассказывали про «жаркую осень: Later I was told about the "hot autumn", when nearly everyone at Mirafiori downed tools.

exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Иврее появ: Later I was told how the portable Lettera 22 came out in Ivrea.
exact.В сорок четвёртом, когда в городе стояли: In '44, while the Americans were in the city, Vesuvius woke up. It felt as if, after everything else, the mountain had decided to remind us it was there too.

exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как жителей Сасс: Later I was told how the people of the Sassi were moved to the new districts.
exact.Когда в Риме были Олимпийские игры, горо: When Rome had the Olympic Games, the city spoke every language at once. We went to look at the foreigners at least, since we hadn't got tickets for the events.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как Рим принимал: Later I was told how Rome hosted the Olympic Games.

exact.В пятидесятые в Сесто ехали с юга, целым: In the fifties people came to Sesto from the south, whole families, with suitcases and boxes. You heard so many dialects on the stairs that I started understanding half of Italy without going anywhere.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сесто ехал: Later I was told how people came to Sesto from the south to work.
